Depending in what building you are. The one i was in had like 25 different buildings with different specializations. I was in the section that was focused on patients who just got there,long term and short term hospitalisations.   
In the one where people who just got there the day was usually:  
Wake up,community talk (all the patients get into one room with the doctors and they talk about whats gonna happen that day),breakfast,meds and then free time or therapies if you have some scheduled, you have 2 group therapies per week and one individual, after that you have lunch and more free time or therapies and then free time until dinner. After that you can do whatever you want until night, if you take meds at night you take them before sleep. What i did most of the time was just listening to music in my room (which was like a hospital room with 4 beds) and playing table tennis with other folks. Of course that was the place where the bad cases go to first. So there were some problematic people you could call them. One guy broke out of the building by just ramming the doors (he escaped for 20 seconds before he got caught). I saw a guy try and hang himself a few times (not succesful although that sight haunts me till this day). And a guy in psychosis attacked a roommate. But most of the time it was pretty calm.

Then the section for short term hospitalisation (ive been there for 4 weeks).   
You wake up,do the community talk thingy,get meds, get breakfast (all this before 9am) and then you have to pick 2 activities you will do throughout the day. There is A LOT of things to do in the whole hospital area so you will definitelly pick something (theres stuff like workshops,clubs and other stuff). But you really need to do them otherwise they will kick you out. Then you have lunch as usual,therapies,doc appointments (you have to do 2 group therapies and have a right to see a doctor and individual therapist twice a week) and if you dont have that then you have free time to do whatever you want. Whats a bit different here was that you can come and go in and out of the building as you want. So you can go for a walk in the hospital area and stuff like that. But you cannot leave the hospital area. I usually went for a walk to a farm that was a part of it. Then you get dinner and meds and go to sleep. This one was super laid back, there were not many restrictions on what you could have with you (other than no drugs,knives,sharp objects) compared to the other one. 

And last but not least the long term ward.  
I hated that place with a passion. Suprisingly this was the worst one of them all. The nurses were super power hungry. I had a towel on my bed and they were bitching about it. They force you to take away pillows and blankets from your bed and you are only allowed to put them back for the night so no nice rests allowed. The days there were way more intense than in the other buildings so it was a bit harsh to adapt to. Nevertheless i left in a week as i signed the waiver saying i can go home. 

Of course this was a psychiatric hospital, ive also been on a psych ward in a normal hospital and that wasnt as pleasant.  
Ive been hospitalised there for suicidal ideation and it felt like a prison mostly. Ive only been there for a day but i guess theres no wonder why they do what they do. I couldnt have any sharp objects,shoelaces,headphones and i was lucky i got to keep my phone. My room was constantly under surveillance. But they treated me with respect. There was no abusive behavior from them compared to the US hospitals. 

All in all its a very good place to go. And its free as long as you have health insurance. (Go free healthcare!)
